content: What is the Leader Completeness property in Raft and why does it prevent committed entries from being lost?

The **Leader Completeness** property is a core safety invariant in the Raft consensus protocol. It states that **if a log entry is committed in a given term, that entry will be present in the logs of the leaders for all higher-numbered terms** [Page 8].

### Why It Prevents Committed Entries from Being Lost:
1. **No Overwriting by Leaders:** In Raft, a leader never overwrites or deletes entries in its own log; it only appends new ones. 
2. **Election Restriction:** Raft's leader election process ensures that a candidate can only be elected if its log is at least as up-to-date as a majority of the cluster. Because a committed entry must exist on a majority of servers, any winning leader must contain that committed entry (or a more recent one) to secure a majority of votes.
3. **Log Preservation:** Since any newly elected leader in a higher term is guaranteed to have all previously committed entries [Page 8], and because of the **Log Matching Property** (which ensures identical preceding entries if index and term match [Page 4]), these committed entries are safely propagated to all other followers and are never overwritten. This guarantees deterministic execution across all replicas in State Machine Replication [Slide 12].
